label: Second unde: a nature actual through an esse other than itself receives that esse
paraphrase: OPEN, analyst formulation of the second 'unde' of ST I q.4 a.1 ad 3 ('Unde non comparatur ad alia sicut recipiens ad receptum: sed magis sicut receptum ad recipiens') and of q.3 a.4 co.'s 'Oportet igitur quod ipsum esse comparetur ad essentiam quae est aliud ab ipso, sicut actus ad potentiam', in its content form at the nature, attribution deferred. This is the STRONG version: its antecedent asks only distinctness of content between the nature and being. Its weaker sibling reads q.3 a.4's 'aliud' as real otherness (registered as strengthens). It bundles (i) real otherness with (ii) reception in the nature. For every x: if x's nature is actual in x through esse (ACTUALIZED_THROUGH_2) and the nature is not being itself, then x's esse is received in that nature as act in receiving potency (RECEPTION_OF_ESSE_1). 'Not being itself' is distinctness of content, which every view considered grants. RECEPTION_OF_ESSE_1 leaves the constitution of the receiving principle open; on the real-composition sense (RECEPTION_OF_ESSE_VERSUS_EXTERNAL_CAUSE_5) Suárez denies it.
